question.text: A ceiling fan having <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> blades of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>80</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> each is rotating with an angular velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1200</mn><mo> </mo><mi>rpm</mi></math>. The magnetic field of earth in that region is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi></math> and angle of dip is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. The emf induced across the blades is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi>π</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> is _______.

solution.text:
Component of the magnetic field perpendicular to the plane of fan blades, Bv=Bsin30°=0.5×10-4 T×12=14×10-4 T

Angular frequency, ω=2π×f=2π60×1200 rad s-1=40π rad s-1

Therefore, induced EMF

ε=12BVωl2=12×14×10-4×40π×0.82

=32π×10-5 V
